name: Irodori-TTS
tagline: Flow-matching Japanese TTS with zero-shot cloning, emoji style cues and automatic duration.
license: Code MIT. Check each model card for weight licenses.

reference.recommended: Several clean clips of the same speaker, about 30 s in total

suggested.label: v4.1 Small (0.8B)
suggested.note: Default. Fast, fp32 on GPU, about 3 GB.

suggested.label: v4.1 Small MeanFlow
suggested.note: Distilled for 4-step sampling. Much faster, slightly less flexible.

suggested.label: v4 Large (3.3B)
suggested.note: Highest quality. 13 GB download, runs in bf16 on 12 GB GPUs.

options.label: Auto
options.help: bf16 when the weights are stored in bf16, are quantized, or would not fit in VRAM as fp32. fp32 otherwise.

options.label: fp32
options.help: Full precision. Reference quality for Small models, needs 4 bytes per parameter of VRAM.

options.label: bf16
options.help: Half the VRAM and usually faster on RTX GPUs. Needed for Large on 12 GB cards.

help.summary: Numeric precision of the diffusion transformer. Changing it reloads the model.
help.increase: fp32 is the most faithful to training but doubles VRAM use.
help.decrease: bf16 halves VRAM and speeds up sampling with a very small quality difference.
help.tip: Keep Auto unless you are comparing quality. Large (3.3B) only fits a 12 GB GPU in bf16.

options.label: fp32
options.help: Recommended. The DACVAE codec is small, so fp32 costs little.

options.label: bf16
options.help: Saves a little VRAM. Can add slight artifacts to encoding and decoding.

help.summary: Precision of the DACVAE codec that encodes the reference and decodes the generated latents into a waveform.
help.increase: fp32 gives the cleanest decode.
help.decrease: bf16 saves a few hundred MB of VRAM.
help.tip: Leave at fp32 unless VRAM is extremely tight.

help.summary: How many candidates to generate in one batched pass. With Seed -1 every take gets its own random seed. With a fixed seed, take n uses seed + n - 1.
help.increase: More variations to choose from. VRAM use and time grow roughly linearly.
help.decrease: Faster and lighter.
help.tip: Generate 2 to 4 takes and keep the best one. Delivery varies a lot between samples.

help.summary: Random seed for the starting noise. -1 picks a new random seed for every take.
help.increase: Any fixed value reproduces the same result with the same model, text, reference and settings.
help.decrease: -1 gives a fresh variation on every run.
help.tip: Each take shows its own seed on the result card. Click it to reproduce that take as Take 1, then tweak other settings with the seed fixed.

help.summary: Number of Euler steps that turn noise into speech latents. 0 uses the checkpoint default (40 for normal models, 4 for MeanFlow).
help.increase: Smoother, more detailed audio up to a point. Time grows linearly with steps.
help.decrease: Faster but can sound grainy or slurred. Combine low values with the Sway schedule.
help.tip: This is the main speed/quality knob. 40 is a good default. Try 8 to 12 with Sway for drafts.

options.label: Linear
options.help: Evenly spaced steps. Best with the default 40 steps.

options.label: Sway
options.help: Spends more steps near the noisy start. Keeps quality when you use few steps.

help.summary: How the sampling steps are spread between noise and the final audio.
help.increase: Sway keeps low step counts usable.
help.decrease: Linear is the reference behavior.
help.tip: Use Sway only together with a low step count (6 to 12).

help.summary: Shape of the Sway schedule. Only used when the timestep schedule is Sway.
help.increase: Values toward +1 move resolution toward the clean end (fine detail).
help.decrease: Values toward -1 move resolution toward the noisy end (overall structure). -1 is the recommended value.
help.tip: Leave at -1 unless you are experimenting.

help.summary: Classifier-free guidance strength for the reference voice. Controls how hard the model pulls toward the reference speaker.
help.increase: Closer timbre and speaking style to the reference. Too high can exaggerate quirks, add noise from the reference or sound strained.
help.decrease: More natural and stable, but the voice drifts toward a generic speaker. 0 disables speaker guidance.
help.tip: If the clone does not sound like the reference, raise this to 6 or 7 first, then try Speaker K/V scale.

help.summary: Guidance strength for the input text. Controls how strictly pronunciation follows the text.
help.increase: Clearer, more accurate pronunciation. Too high sounds robotic or rushed.
help.decrease: Looser, more relaxed delivery but more mumbling or skipped words.
help.tip: Raise slightly (3.5 to 4.5) if words are slurred or dropped.

settings.label: Style caption
settings.placeholder: e.g. 落ち着いた声で、ゆっくり優しく話している

help.summary: Optional natural-language description of the delivery (emotion, pace, situation). Combined with the reference voice on checkpoints that support captions (v4.1 Small and v3 VoiceDesign).
help.increase: A specific caption steers emotion and pacing while the reference keeps the identity.
help.decrease: Leave empty to copy the delivery from the reference audio only.
help.tip: Write it in Japanese. Ignored by checkpoints without caption conditioning (the result card will say so).

help.summary: Guidance strength for the style caption. Only used when a caption is given.
help.increase: The caption's emotion and pace come through more strongly, possibly at the cost of speaker similarity.
help.decrease: The caption becomes a light hint and the reference style dominates.
help.tip: Balance it against Speaker guidance. If the voice changes identity, lower this.

options.label: Independent
options.help: Each condition gets its own guidance branch. Most flexible, uses the most VRAM and compute.

options.label: Joint
options.help: Drops all conditions together. 2x compute, but all enabled guidance scales must be equal.

options.label: Alternating
options.help: Guides one condition per step in rotation. 2x compute, slightly weaker per-condition control.

help.summary: How classifier-free guidance is computed when several conditions (text, speaker, caption) are active.
help.increase: Independent gives separate control of every scale.
help.decrease: Joint or Alternating lower the per-step cost when VRAM or speed matters.
help.tip: Keep Independent. Joint fails if the scales differ.

help.summary: Guidance is only applied while the timestep t is between min t and max t (t = 1 is pure noise, t = 0 is the final audio).
help.increase: Guidance stops earlier, so the final detail is left to the model. More natural, less adherence.
help.decrease: Guidance stays active until the end. Stronger adherence, more risk of harshness.
help.tip: 0.5 is the trained default.

help.summary: Upper timestep bound for guidance. 1.0 means guidance starts at the very first step.
help.increase: 1.0 guides the global structure (rhythm, identity) from the beginning.
help.decrease: Lower values skip guidance at the noisiest steps and loosen the overall structure.
help.tip: Leave at 1.0.

help.summary: Experimental. Multiplies the attention keys and values coming from the reference speaker, which strengthens speaker identity without raising guidance.
help.increase: 1.1 to 1.5 can noticeably improve similarity. Large values distort the audio.
help.decrease: 0 (off) or 1.0 leaves the model unchanged.
help.tip: Try 1.2 when the voice drifts from the reference even with higher Speaker guidance.

help.summary: Speaker K/V scaling is applied only while t is at or above this value (the early, noisy steps).
help.increase: Closer to 1 limits the effect to the first steps (identity only).
help.decrease: Lower values keep scaling active longer, which affects fine detail and can add artifacts.
help.tip: 0.9 is the documented default.

help.summary: Limits Speaker K/V scaling to the first N transformer layers. 0 applies it to all layers.
help.increase: More layers give a stronger effect.
help.decrease: Fewer layers give a gentler, more targeted effect.
help.tip: Only matters when Speaker K/V scale is on.

help.summary: Exact output length in seconds. 0 lets the built-in duration predictor choose the length. When the length is above 20 s, the text is split into parts and the length is spread over them in proportion to their predicted durations.
help.increase: Longer than natural makes speech slow with long pauses or trailing noise.
help.decrease: Shorter than natural makes speech rushed or cut off.
help.tip: Prefer Auto plus Duration scale. Use a fixed length only for timing to video. Silence trimming and the pauses between parts can make split output slightly shorter or longer than the value.

help.summary: Multiplies the predicted duration. A simple way to control speaking rate.
help.increase: Above 1 gives slower, more spacious speech.
help.decrease: Below 1 gives faster speech. Too low drops syllables.
help.tip: 0.9 to 1.15 sounds natural. If the end of a sentence is cut off, raise it to 1.1.

help.summary: Upper limit on the length of one generated part. Text predicted to be longer than 20 s, or longer than this value if it is lower, is split at sentence boundaries, generated part by part and joined automatically.
help.increase: Values of 20 s and above all behave the same, because parts never exceed 20 s. Irodori-TTS was trained on utterances of up to 30 s and breaks down beyond that.
help.decrease: Below 20 s the text is split into shorter parts. Each part is more stable, but intonation is carried across fewer sentences.
help.tip: Leave it at 20 s or more. Long text is handled by splitting, so there is no need to raise this.

help.summary: Scales the starting noise. Values below 1 pull samples toward the average.
help.increase: Closer to 1 (or off) keeps full variety and expressiveness.
help.decrease: 0.8 to 0.9 gives more consistent, safer takes with less expression.
help.tip: Useful when takes are unstable. 0 disables it.

help.summary: Temporal score rescaling strength. Must be set together with Score rescale sigma, otherwise both are ignored.
help.increase: Stronger rescaling changes the sharpness of the result.
help.decrease: 0 disables the feature.
help.tip: Experimental. Leave off unless you know you need it.

help.summary: Noise level parameter for temporal score rescaling. Pairs with Score rescale k.
help.increase: Applies the rescaling over a wider noise range.
help.decrease: 0 disables the feature.
help.tip: Experimental.

help.summary: Normalizes each reference clip to a target loudness before encoding, as was done when the codec was trained.
help.increase: On is recommended. Quiet or loud recordings are handled consistently.
help.decrease: Off keeps the raw level, which can make the clone too quiet, too loud or noisy.
help.tip: Keep on.

help.summary: Loudness the reference is normalized to.
help.increase: Louder reference level.
help.decrease: Quieter reference level.
help.tip: -16 dB matches training. Changing it rarely helps.

help.summary: Maximum combined reference length. Clips are joined in order and cut at this length. 0 uses the checkpoint value (120 s for v4).
help.increase: Longer references add more speaker evidence, with diminishing returns after about 30 s.
help.decrease: Shorter references are faster to process but capture less of the voice.
help.tip: Clip order matters. Put your best clip first.

help.summary: Rewrites English words, acronyms and your dictionary entries as katakana before the text reaches the model, so that Irodori-TTS reads them like a Japanese speaker would (Graphical User Interface becomes グラフィカルユーザーインターフェース, GUI becomes ジーユーアイ). The Reading box under the text shows the result and lets you change any word.
help.increase: On reads mixed Japanese and English text naturally. Irodori-TTS was trained on Japanese text only and garbles raw English.
help.decrease: Off sends the text exactly as typed.
help.tip: Click a word in the Reading box to pick another reading or save it to the dictionary. Manage the dictionary in Models > Reading.

help.summary: Lets the d1-omni-600M decision model choose between readings that depend on context, such as sake (サケ or セイク), live (ライブ or リブ) and No. (ナンバー or ノー). It runs on the CPU, so it never takes VRAM from the TTS model.
help.increase: On picks the reading from the whole sentence. The first use loads the model in about 5 to 10 s.
help.decrease: Off always uses the most common reading. Only these words are affected, everything else is converted the same way.
help.tip: Set it up once in Models > Reading (about 2.4 GB). It is right roughly 4 times out of 5, so check the highlighted words in the Reading box.

help.summary: Cuts trailing near-silent latent frames after the speech ends.
help.increase: On removes dead air at the end.
help.decrease: Off keeps the full predicted length. Turn it off if the last syllable gets clipped.
help.tip: Mostly matters for older v2 checkpoints.

help.summary: Upstream Irodori-TTS embeds a SilentCipher digital watermark in every waveform it returns. Turning this on skips that step and saves takes exactly as the model produced them.
help.increase: On generates and saves the audio without the watermark payload. Nothing else about generation changes.
help.decrease: Off keeps the upstream behavior: every take carries the SilentCipher mark. This is the default.
help.tip: Leave off unless you need unmarked audio. The mark is near-inaudible and survives re-encoding.

options.label: Sequential
options.help: Decodes takes one at a time. Lowest VRAM.

options.label: Batch
options.help: Decodes all takes together. Faster with several takes, more VRAM.

help.summary: How multiple takes are decoded from latents into audio.
help.increase: Batch is faster for 2 or more takes.
help.decrease: Sequential avoids VRAM spikes.
help.tip: No effect on quality.

help.summary: Precomputes attention keys and values for the text, speaker and caption once per generation.
help.increase: On is faster.
help.decrease: Off only for debugging or numerical comparisons.
help.tip: Keep on.
